name: Doubling Time (Rule of 72)
description: Approximate how long a quantity takes to double at a given annual growth rate.
business_contexts: an investor estimating how long a portfolio takes to double
a company estimating how long revenue takes to double at its current growth rate
a demographer estimating how long a population takes to double
a lender estimating how long a balance takes to double at a given rate
a startup estimating how long its user base takes to double
question_patterns: Using the Rule of 72, approximately how many years will it take to double at the growth rate given below?
Given the annual growth rate below, approximately how long will it take to double?
Using the Rule of 72, calculate the approximate doubling time for the growth rate shown.
At the growth rate given below, roughly how many years until the quantity doubles?
Approximately how many years does the growth rate below take to double a value?
key_insight: The Rule of 72 is a mental-math shortcut, not an exact formula — it trades precision for something you can compute in your head under time pressure.
common_mistakes: Dividing 72 by the decimal rate (e.g. 0.08) instead of the rate expressed as a whole percentage number (8)
Forgetting the answer is an approximation, not an exact compounding calculation
framework_soundbite: 72 divided by the growth rate — a fast, good-enough answer to 'how long until this doubles?'
